title: M3 Wear OS Apps Design Kit

components.caption: Highest emphasis; the screen's primary action.
The kit's highlighted style — a filled button in the variant palette.
Medium emphasis, on a tonal container.
Medium emphasis, drawn as an outline over the background.
Lowest emphasis; no container at all, for a button inside another surface.
A short button for a dense screen, with the kit's content and style axes folded in.
A button over an image, with the scrim that keeps its label legible.
A button waiting on the work it started — the kit's loading pattern.
Buttons that share a row and expand away from whichever one is pressed.
components.noReference: The kit publishes no button-group set — it draws rows as side-by-side instances of its button sets. This is a Wear Compose component with no kit counterpart.

components.caption: The plain container: one content slot, tonal by default. A no-`onClick` overload presents the same card without the tap.
The kit's outline style — the same container drawn as a border.
A card led by a title, with the kit's numbered layouts folded in as content cells.
A card that names the app it came from — the shape a notification takes.
Interrupts to ask for a decision; the kit's button arrangements fold in as cells.
Hands the task to the paired phone, with the progress the wait needs.
The screen-hugging confirm action, curved to the bottom edge of the display.
Highest emphasis; an icon-only action.
The kit's highlighted style — a filled icon button in the variant palette.
Medium emphasis, on a tonal container.
Medium emphasis, drawn as an outline over the background.
Lowest emphasis; the kit's child style, with no container at all.
A short label as a round action, with the kit's style and size axes folded in.
Where the screen sits in a scroll, drawn against the right bezel.
The value a rotating side button is setting, while it is being turned.
Which page of a horizontal pager is showing, along the bottom of the display.
The same indicator for a vertical pager, drawn against the right bezel.
The Wear list: rows scale and fade toward the edges of the round display.
components.noReference: The kit publishes no list set — its list pages are the row components (list header, cards) rather than the scrolling container. This is the Wear Compose list idiom, and the transformation that scales and fades rows against the bezel is only visible on the real one.

components.caption: The screen frame: curved clock, scroll position, and the bottom action, in their places.
components.noReference: The kit publishes no scaffold: the chrome it arranges — the curved clock, the scroll indicator, the edge button — are separate sets, and the thing that places them is Wear Compose's, not the kit's.

components.caption: Three wheels for a date, with the kit's field orderings folded in.
Wheels for a time, pinned to 10:10; the kit's clock formats fold in as cells.
One wheel of options — the primitive the date and time pickers are built from.
A button whose label has not arrived yet.
An icon button whose icon has not arrived yet.
A card whose content has not arrived yet.
A ring around the display edge, with the kit's progress and stroke axes folded in.
The same ring cut into segments, for progress through a countable set of steps.
An indeterminate arc along the bezel, for a wait with no measurable progress.
components.noReference: The kit publishes no arc indicator: its progress sets are the full ring, the segmented ring and the linear track. This is a Wear Compose component with no kit counterpart.

components.caption: A straight track, for progress inside a component or a list row.
A labelled row that toggles a checkbox; for a set where any number may be chosen.
A labelled row that flips a switch; for a setting that takes effect immediately.
A labelled row in a set where exactly one may be chosen.
The expressive shape library, with each named shape folded in as a variant.
A value across a fixed number of steps, with the kit's levels folded in as cells.
A value moved a step at a time, between buttons at the top and bottom of the screen.
A card swiped aside to show its actions.
The same gesture over a button rather than a card.
Titles the screen a list belongs to; the first thing above the list.
Divides a long list into named runs, without leaving the screen's title behind.
Running text at the `bodyMedium` role of the Wear type scale.
Secondary text at the `labelSmall` role — a timestamp, a unit, a footnote.
The curved status strip every Wear screen carries, pinned to a fixed time.
An icon that holds an on/off state, with the kit's size and state axes folded in.
A short label that holds an on/off state.
